caption.scope: Only requests that reached the router are counted. Calls that the gateway fallback served while the router was failing are not.
caption.unmetered: {count, plural, one {# unmetered call: its stream ended before usage arrived. It is not in the cost above. Approximate upper bound: {upperBound}.} other {# unmetered calls: their streams ended before usage arrived. They are not in the cost above. Approximate upper bound: {upperBound}.}}
caption.unmetered.help: The bound is approximate: the estimated prompt at the uncached input price, plus the requested output cap at the output price. The prompt is estimated at 4 characters per token, so the bound can be too low for Chinese, Japanese or Korean text.
caption.unmetered.partial.help: Some of these calls set no output cap, so their bound covers input only. The total may be well below the real cost.
caption.listPrice: List price from the {region} price catalog {catalogVersion}. This is not your AWS invoice: discounts, credits and taxes are not included.
caption.retention: Request records are kept {days} days. Daily totals are kept {rollupDays} days.
caption.noContent: Prompt and output text are never stored.
term.tier: Tier: fast, standard or frontier. Each tier maps to models in the routing policy.
term.observe: Observe: the router serves a fixed default model and only logs what it would choose.
term.auto: Auto: the router serves the model it chooses.
term.session: Session: one agent session, identified by its session header. Shown as a short label, never the raw id.
term.lineage: Lineage: one agent's chain of requests in a session. Sub-agents get their own lineage.
term.breakPoint: Cache break point: a moment when the prompt cache is cold anyway (session start, sub-agent start, idle past the TTL, compaction). The router switches models only at these points.
term.hardLock: Hard lock: the router keeps the current model (tool loop, response chain, or state another model cannot read).
term.costGate: Cost gate: a downgrade must save more over the next calls than the cold write it causes.
term.coldWrite: Cold write: writing the whole context into the cache of a new model after a switch.
term.hitRate: Cache hit rate: cache read tokens divided by prompt tokens.
term.listPrice: List price: the price in the region's price catalog. Not your invoice.
term.baseline: Baseline: what the same tokens would cost on a fixed choice of model.
term.caller: Caller: the member or service client that sent the request.
term.unattributed: Unattributed: the request had no valid identity header, so the router could not tell who sent it.
term.pin: Pin: the client asked for a specific model with x-router-hint: pin=<model id>.
term.failover: Failover: the router retried on another inference profile or a sibling model after an error.
term.fallback: Gateway fallback: the gateway served the request with fixed models because the router failed or was unreachable.
term.assessor: Assessor: an optional LLM that proposes a tier for a turn. In observe mode its answer is only logged.
term.pack: Pack: the assessor's prompt and rules, bundled in the router image.
term.wouldChoose: Would choose: the model auto mode would have served. Logged in observe mode.

savings.title: Savings
savings.description: What routing changed in list-price cost, against a baseline.
savings.baseline.static.help: Each request is priced on the model of the tier it asked for: auto uses the pool's default tier, auto:fast uses fast. Tiers the client chose itself save nothing.
savings.baseline.observeDefault.help: In observe mode this equals actual, so the net saving is minus the assessor overhead.
savings.baseline.help: A baseline prices the same requests on one fixed model that never switches, from the same API's pool.
savings.kpi.routing.help: R = B − A*: the price difference between the baseline model and the served model, with cold-cache effects removed.
savings.kpi.switchPenalty.help: S = A − A*: extra cache writes when routing moved a warm lineage to another model.
savings.kpi.assessor.help: X: what the assessor's own calls cost.
savings.kpi.netFormula: Net saving N = B − A − X = R − S − X
savings.kpi.cache.help: Cnet: what the same tokens would cost with no caching, minus actual cost, net of the cache-write premium. This comes from prompt caching, not from routing.
savings.matrix.title: Where requests went
savings.matrix.help: Requests by baseline tier and served tier, with their routing effect.
savings.otherCold.help: Cache writes after switches that routing did not choose: failover, a policy change, a client pin. Not in the net saving.
savings.capRow.help: Requests served at a lower tier because of a tier limit. A forced downgrade is not a routing saving, so it is shown on its own.
savings.projected.count: {count, plural, one {# request where auto would have chosen another model} other {# requests where auto would have chosen another model}}
savings.caption.listPrice: All figures are list prices ({catalogVersion}), not your invoice.
savings.caption.sameUsage: Same usage is assumed: the baseline prices the same token counts at the baseline model's price. A different model may use more or fewer tokens and turns.
savings.caption.quality: Quality is not measured. A cheaper model may solve fewer tasks. In our coding-agent benchmarks the fast tier solved 14–17 points fewer tasks than standard.
savings.caption.observe: Observe mode: the router serves the observe default, so the figures show only how that model differs from the baseline. "Projected if auto" estimates what auto would have cost.
savings.caption.projection: Indicative, not measured: the same tokens repriced on the models auto would have chosen, carried forward along each lineage. Exact for the shipped policy; approximate when user turns are cost-gated.
savings.caption.evidence: Benchmark evidence: on two coding benchmarks, auto with the assessor cost 2.6–4.1 times fixed standard, with no quality gain detected.
savings.caption.unmetered: {count, plural, one {# unmetered call is left out of these figures.} other {# unmetered calls are left out of these figures.}}
savings.empty.observeBaseline: With the observe default as baseline in observe mode, actual equals baseline. The net saving is minus the assessor overhead. Open "Projected if auto" or pick another baseline.

getStarted.title: Get started
getStarted.intro: Connect your coding agent or your code to the router. You sign in with your own account. No shared secret and no AWS credentials are needed.
getStarted.values.title: This deployment
getStarted.values.missing: This deployment is not fully configured. Ask an admin.
getStarted.values.missingAdmin: Missing value: {name}. Set it in the stack and deploy again.
getStarted.step1.title: 1. Install llmar
getStarted.step1.body: llmar is one Python 3 file with no dependencies outside the standard library. llmar-token and llmar-login are links to it, so tools can call them with no arguments.
getStarted.step1.source: It is published in the project repository. The console does not serve files.
getStarted.configure.title: 2. Configure it for this deployment
getStarted.configure.body: This saves the deployment's values in ~/.config/llmar/config.json: sign-in domain, client id, scope, callback ports and gateway URL. The file holds no secrets.
getStarted.step2.title: 3. Sign in
getStarted.step2.body: llmar login opens your browser at the sign-in page. Sign in with your password. llmar then saves a refresh token in ~/.config/llmar/. Only you can read the file.
getStarted.step2.mfa: First sign-in: replace the temporary password from the invite e-mail with your own.
getStarted.step2.again: Sign in again after {refreshDays} days, after "Sign out everywhere", or after an admin re-enabled your account.
getStarted.step2.noBrowser: No browser on this machine (for example over SSH)? Run llmar login --no-browser. It prints a link and an ssh -L command. Forward the port, then open the link on your own computer.
getStarted.step2.test: Test: llmar status shows who you are and when your token expires.
getStarted.step3.title: 4. Set up your tool
getStarted.step3.identity: Send the token twice: as Authorization: Bearer and as x-api-key. The gateway checks the first. The router reads the second to record you as the caller.
getStarted.claudeCode.token: apiKeyHelper runs llmar-token. Claude Code sends the token as a bearer token and as x-api-key. With the TTL at 4 minutes it asks often; llmar answers from its cache and refreshes the token before it expires.
getStarted.claudeCode.tiers: The alias variables make /model opus, sonnet and haiku ask the router for a tier. Claude Code shows an unrecognized_model notice for auto. You can ignore it.
getStarted.claudeCode.countTokens: The gateway does not offer /v1/messages/count_tokens. Claude Code gets a 404 and uses its own estimate.
getStarted.claudeCode.refusal: If the model refuses on safety grounds, Claude Code may retry with its built-in fallback model. That id is not routable, so the retry fails.
getStarted.codex.auth: Codex runs llmar-token for the Authorization header and refreshes it every 4 minutes. Use the absolute path: Codex does not expand ~.
getStarted.codex.oauth: For x-api-key, Codex signs you in a second time in its own browser window. This is how the router records you as the caller. So you sign in once to llmar and once to Codex.
getStarted.codex.ssh: Over SSH, Codex's own sign-in needs its callback port forwarded too: ssh -L {port}:127.0.0.1:{port} <host>. Codex prints the sign-in URL; open it on your own computer.
getStarted.codex.keyring: Headless Linux without a keyring: add credentials_store = "file" to the gateway_oauth table. Codex then keeps its sign-in in $CODEX_HOME/secrets/gateway_oauth.json (mode 0600, plain text).
getStarted.codex.short: Sessions shorter than 30 minutes can skip the second sign-in. Use the provider table below instead, and leave out the auth and gateway_oauth tables: one token is read at start and sent in both headers.
getStarted.codex.webSearch: Web search must stay off. With it on, Bedrock ends every stream with an error and Codex retries until it gives up.
getStarted.codex.warning: The warning "Model metadata for 'auto' not found" is harmless. That is why the context window is set by hand.
getStarted.sdk.token: RouterAuth asks llmar for a token on every request and sets both headers. llmar answers from its cache, so this is cheap, and a long-running process never sends an expired token.
getStarted.sdk.session: Use one x-router-session id per agent session. Cache-aware routing depends on it. Never share one id across sessions.
getStarted.sdk.decision: To see which model served a call, read the x-router-model response header (with_raw_response in both SDKs).
getStarted.sdk.stream: Streaming works with the SDKs' usual calls.
getStarted.curl.body: A single call to check the setup. -D - prints the response headers, including x-router-model.
getStarted.step4.title: 5. Check your setup
getStarted.step4.body: Send one request with your tool, then press Check.
getStarted.step4.found: Found your request from {time}: {dialect}, requested {requested}, served by {model}.
getStarted.step4.notFound: No request from you in the last 10 minutes. If you sent one, check that the x-api-key header is set (step 4).
getStarted.step4.require: This deployment requires your identity. A request without x-api-key gets 401 identity-missing.
getStarted.step4.observe: Without x-api-key your requests still work, but they are not recorded as yours.
getStarted.step4.off: Identity is off in this deployment, so requests are not recorded per caller and this check cannot find yours.
getStarted.models.title: Models and tiers in this deployment
getStarted.models.observe: This deployment runs in observe mode. Every auto request is served by the observe default: {observeDefaults}. Tier aliases and tier= hints take effect only in auto mode. A pin= hint works in both modes.
getStarted.models.auto: This deployment runs in auto mode. The router picks a tier for each request and switches models only at cache break points.
getStarted.endpoints.title: Endpoints and headers
getStarted.endpoints.model: Send model auto, or auto:fast, auto:standard or auto:frontier. A concrete model id is treated as a pin: it is served if it is in the routing policy and within your tier limit. Otherwise you get 400 (pin-not-allowed or access-cap).
getStarted.endpoints.headers: The gateway forwards only these request headers: {headers}.
getStarted.endpoints.response: Response headers: x-router-decision, x-router-model (the model that served the call) and x-router-reason.
getStarted.trouble.title: Troubleshooting
getStarted.trouble.401: 401: no token or an expired token. With identity required, also a missing x-api-key (identity-missing) or an invalid one (identity-…).
getStarted.trouble.403: 403 identity-blocked: your account is disabled or blocked. Ask an admin. A 403 without that code means the token has the wrong scope.
getStarted.trouble.pin: 400 pin-not-allowed: the pinned or named model is not in the routing policy.
getStarted.trouble.accessCap: 400 access-cap: the pinned model or model id you asked for is above your tier limit. A tier you ask for above the limit is not an error: you are served at the highest tier you may use. Ask an admin to raise the limit.
getStarted.trouble.accessCapContext: 400 access-cap-context: the conversation is too long for every model within your tier limit. Start a new session or compact the context.
getStarted.trouble.countTokens: 404 on count_tokens: harmless. The client uses its own estimate.
getStarted.trouble.codexStream: Codex "stream disconnected before response.completed": web search is on. Turn it off.
getStarted.trouble.relogin: "run llmar login" (llmar-token exit code 2): your sign-in expired or was revoked, or the settings changed (llmar configure) since you signed in. Run llmar login. If it keeps failing, your account may be disabled.
getStarted.trouble.codexAuth: Codex says "auth command exited with status 2" and nothing more: run llmar-token in a terminal to see why. Usually you need to run llmar login.
getStarted.trouble.idpDown: llmar-token exit code 3: the sign-in service cannot be reached and no usable cached token is left. While the cached token has more than 30 seconds left, llmar still prints it, with a warning.
getStarted.trouble.usage: llmar-token exit code 4: a setup problem, such as missing settings, a credentials file other users can read, the llmar directory or its parent writable by others, or bad usage. The message says which.
getStarted.trouble.budget: 429 budget-exceeded: you are over your monthly budget. Ask an admin.
getStarted.admin.clients: For CI and other automation, create a service client instead of using a member account.
members.title: Members
members.description: People who use the router. They sign in with their own account.
members.col.name: Name
members.invite.name: Name
members.invite.help: Cognito sends an e-mail with a temporary password. The member sets a new password at first sign-in.
members.roleApplies: The new role applies at the router within about 35 seconds.
members.adminSignIn: {name} must sign in again before the admin rights apply.
members.adminSignIn.self: You are now an admin. Sign in again to use the admin pages.
members.signOutEverywhere.confirm: This revokes {name}'s refresh tokens. Their llmar CLI and console sessions must sign in again. Tokens already issued work at the gateway until they expire (up to 30 minutes) unless you also disable the member.
members.disable.title: Disable {name}?
members.disable.body: In require mode the router stops serving {name} within about 35 seconds. In observe mode, requests that carry {name}'s identity are blocked within about 35 seconds, but requests without it are served until the token expires (up to 30 minutes). Their records stay.
members.enable.body: {name} can use the router again within about 35 seconds. They must run llmar login again, because disabling revoked their sign-in.
members.delete.title: Delete {name}?
members.delete.body: Only disabled members can be deleted. Their records stay and show as "Deleted member". This cannot be undone.
members.error.exists: A user with this e-mail already exists.
members.error.self: You cannot disable or delete your own account.
members.error.lastAdmin: This is the last admin. Make someone else an admin first.
members.empty: No members yet. Invite the first one.
budget.title: Budget
budget.hardStop: Stop serving when the budget is used up
budget.hardStop.help: The router answers 429 budget-exceeded within a few minutes after the budget is used up: usage is counted from the router logs, which arrive in batches. Requests in that window still go through, so spend can pass the budget a little. In observe mode this binds only calls that carry x-api-key. Budgets use list price, so they can differ from the invoice.
budget.advisory: In observe mode, budgets bind every call that carries a valid x-api-key. A call without one is served unattributed and escapes them. They bind everyone only in Require.
budget.spendIncludes: Budget spend is actual cost plus assessor cost, for the current UTC month.
clients.title: Service clients
clients.description: Machine callers such as CI jobs and agents. They use the client-credentials flow.
clients.col.name: Name
clients.create.name: Name
clients.limits.help: Budgets and tier limits work as for members. Without its own values, a client has no budget and no tier limit.
clients.secret.title: Client secret
clients.secret.once: Copy the secret now. It is shown only once.
clients.secret.store: Store it in a Secrets Manager secret that only this job can read. Do not put it in config files.
clients.secret.script: The machine token script from the README reads the secret and prints a token. Send it as Authorization: Bearer and as x-api-key:
clients.rotate.body: A new secret is created. Update the job before you remove the old one.
clients.disable.body: The router stops serving this client within about 35 seconds. In observe mode this holds only for calls that send x-api-key.
clients.delete.body: Records stay. This cannot be undone.
clients.empty: No service clients. Members use their own account; service clients are for automation.

config.valid: Valid. Nothing is active until you activate it.
config.invalid: {count, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}} found.

config.activate.body: The router picks it up within about 1 minute. Sessions keep their current model until their next cache break point.
config.effects.title: Effect on running sessions
config.effects.none: No running session changes model because of this.
config.effects.list: {count, plural, one {# change can move sessions at their next cache break point:} other {# changes can move sessions at their next cache break point:}}
config.effects.cannotCompare: The active config no longer passes validation, for example because a model left the price catalog. So the effect on running sessions cannot be computed. Check the whole change before you activate it.
config.conflict: Someone activated version {version} while you were editing. Review their change first.
config.rollback.body: This creates a new version with the content of version {version}.

policy.title: Routing policy
policy.description: Which models serve each tier, and how the router chooses.
policy.whatIf.later: Replaying recent decisions under a draft comes in a later release.
policy.mode.help: Observe serves the observe default and logs what auto would choose. Auto serves the chosen model.
policy.autoWarning: In auto mode the router serves the model it chooses. Check the Savings projection and the benchmark evidence first.
policy.observeDefaults.help: The model that serves each API in observe mode.
policy.aliases.help: Model names clients may send, and the tier each one asks for.
policy.aliases.name: Name
policy.rules.help: Rules set the desired tier for matching requests. The first match wins.
policy.sessionTier.help: When on, the whole session takes the tier chosen at its start.
access.title: Tier limits
access.help: Limit the highest tier a group or a caller may use. Applies within about 35 seconds. It also limits the observe default, would-choose and projected models.
access.allowPins.help: Empty: a pin is allowed when its tier is within the limit. A listed model is allowed even above the limit.
access.precedence: A caller's own limit wins over the group default.
access.advisory: In observe mode, tier limits bind every call that carries a valid x-api-key. A call without one is served unattributed and escapes them.
assessor.title: Assessor
assessor.description: An optional LLM that proposes a tier at the start of a turn.
assessor.mode.help: Off: never called. Observe: called, answer only logged. Auto: the answer can change the served model.
assessor.autoWarning: In auto mode the assessor's tier changes the served model. In our benchmarks no ability to pick the tasks that need frontier was detected, and it never chose fast. Keep observe until the offline evaluation passes.
assessor.autoConfirm: I have read the evidence and want auto mode.
assessor.pack.bundled: Only packs bundled in the router image can be chosen.
assessor.threshold.help: An answer below this confidence is treated as no opinion.
assessor.autoRules: Rules that may act in auto mode
assessor.savesConfig: Saving creates a new config version. The routing policy in it is unchanged.
assessor.rules.title: Rules in {pack}
assessor.rules.textNote: Rule text is shown as written in the pack.
assessor.stats.title: Activity
gateway.title: Gateway
gateway.description: The AgentCore Gateway in front of the router. Most settings change only with a CDK deploy.
gateway.authorizer.scopesOnly: The gateway checks the token and its scope. The router checks who the caller is.
gateway.rules.all: Every model name goes to the router (a lowest-priority catch-all rule).
gateway.rules.fallback: If the router answers 5xx or cannot be reached, the gateway serves the request with the fallback models.
health.title: Health
health.description: Is the router serving well right now.
health.tasksZero: The router has 0 tasks. Requests go to the gateway fallback.
health.fallbackSigns.help: The gateway publishes no fallback count. These signs mean requests may have gone to the fallback models: router 5xx, unhealthy router targets, and fewer running tasks than desired.
audit.title: Audit log
audit.description: Every admin action, with who, when and what changed.
audit.action.member.update: Changed a member's budget or tier limit
audit.action.config.redeliver: Republished a config version to the router
audit.readOnly: The audit log cannot be edited.
audit.empty: No admin actions in this period.
settings.title: Settings
settings.mfa.off: Off in this deployment. For production, require TOTP MFA on the user pool. It is a stack setting: see infra/README.md, "Production hardening: MFA".
settings.signOutEverywhere.body: Signs you out of every browser and revokes your llmar CLI sign-in. The CLI notices at its next refresh, within 30 minutes, and the gateway accepts tokens already issued until they expire. Run llmar login again afterwards.
settings.signOutEverywhere.done: You are signed out everywhere, including the llmar CLI. Sign in again here, and run llmar login for your tools.
settings.identity.help: Whether the router needs to know the caller. Require rejects requests without a valid x-api-key.
settings.identity.requireWarning: Clients that do not send x-api-key will get 401. Check the Unattributed share on the Overview first.
settings.identity.observeNote: In observe mode, blocks, budgets and tier limits apply to every call that carries a valid x-api-key. A call without one is served unattributed and escapes them. They bind everyone only in Require.
settings.identity.requireBlocked: You cannot switch to Require yet. The router has not reported that its signing keys are loaded. Without them, every call would get 401.
settings.retention.help: Set at deploy time (recordRetentionDays). A change applies to new records. Daily totals are kept 400 days.
settings.cdkOnly: Set at deploy time. Change it with a CDK deploy.
settings.saved: Saved. It applies within about 1 minute.
auth.noRole: Your account has no role yet. Ask an admin.

ext.getStarted.step4.unknown: The identity mode of this deployment is not known right now. Set x-api-key so that your requests are recorded as yours.
ext.state.configUnavailable: The deploy-time settings cannot be read. The router keeps running on its current config. Retry, or check the router stack deploy.
ext.effects.identityWeakened: The identity mode goes down. Calls without a valid x-api-key will be served, and blocks, budgets and tier limits will not apply to them. In Off, they apply to no call.
ext.effects.identityStrengthened: The identity mode goes up. In Require, a call without a valid x-api-key gets 401. Check the unattributed share on the Overview first.
ext.effects.assessorMode: The assessor mode changes. In Auto, the assessor's tier can change the served model; in Observe or Off, it cannot.
ext.identityKeys.count: {total, plural, one {Signing keys loaded on {withKeys} of # router task} other {Signing keys loaded on {withKeys} of # router tasks}}
ext.identityKeys.reason.noFreshTask: No router task has reported in the last 15 minutes, so the console cannot confirm that the keys are loaded. Check on the Health page that the router is running.
ext.identityKeys.reason.partial: Not every running router task has reported in the last 15 minutes, or the number of running tasks could not be read, for example during a deploy. Try again in a few minutes.
ext.identityKeys.reason.notConfigured: Router task {task} has no identity configured, so it cannot check x-api-key. Check the router stack identity settings.
ext.identityKeys.reason.taskWithoutKeys: Router task {task} has not loaded the signing keys. Try again in a minute. If it does not change, check the hourly key sync (jwks-sync) in the router stack.
